note: Twelve segments chosen by hand from the TRAINING split, so the test split stays untouched. List order is case order. The label is not written here: build_examples.py reads it from the dataset. The "why" is our own reading of the plot, checked against the samples; OPSSAT-AD does not publish a cause per anomaly.

cases.why: The usual smooth magnetometer arc; the small spikes are noise of at most 0.7e-5 (ten times smaller than the jumps in this channel's anomalies), there are no stretches stuck at zero and everything stays within the nominal range.

Between t=185 and t=195 s two consecutive samples shoot to -5.2e-5 and +6.3e-5 (a 1.15e-4 jump, about 75 times the typical step) and the signal returns to the arc: a slowly varying magnetic field does not do that, and +6.3e-5 exceeds the maximum of every nominal segment in the channel (5.0e-5).
A clean photodiode bell up to 1.05 rad; the falling tail is slow and straight but has no jumps or steps, and it ends at zero, the channel's usual resting value.

It leaves zero abruptly (0 to 0.06 rad in two samples), sits on a noisy plateau near 0.1 rad and drops in a step at t=114-115 s, never forming the smooth bell; its maximum (0.12) is far below what is normal for the channel (95% of nominal segments exceed 0.44).

The first 21 s are stuck at exactly 0 and the next sample jumps to -3.2e-5 to follow the normal arc: a frozen or lost reading at the start, since the real magnetometer never reads a sustained exact zero.
A textbook smooth magnetometer arc between -3.5e-5 and +3.0e-5, with no zeros or jumps (the largest step between samples is 0.2e-5).

A shoulder, a smooth peak up to 0.60 rad (right at the channel median) and a fast but continuous fall to zero; the zeros at the start and the end are the photodiode's normal resting value, not lost readings.

In the middle of the arc there are two stretches stuck at exactly 0 (t=44-94 s and t=127-142 s) and, coming back from the second, a single-sample spike to 6.3e-5, above the maximum of every nominal segment in the channel (5.0e-5).
Right at the peak (0.52 rad) a single sample drops to 0.33 at t=65 s and the next one is back at 0.52: a one-point notch in a curve that should be smooth.
A smooth magnetometer arc with only 21 samples because this stretch arrives every 5 s; having few samples is not an anomaly and there are no jumps or zeros.

Before the peak there is a stray 13 s pulse (t=175-187 s) that returns to exactly zero for 22 s, and the main peak starts abruptly and is jagged, with sharp drops; the low amplitude (0.12 rad) is not the reason, because this channel has nominal segments just as low.

Hard on purpose: it is noisy, only reaches 0.40 rad and has a small spike at t=120 s, but it follows a single bell with no zero stretches inside the peak and no large back-and-forth jumps, and the annotators labelled it nominal; noisy is not the same as anomalous.
